source_document.body:
Small online sellers are raising free-shipping minimums, charging for returns and absorbing higher label costs as the U.S. Postal Service moves to make its fuel surcharge permanent. USPS filed notice Nov. 12 to convert the 8% charge it added to package prices in April into an 11% fuel surcharge on Jan. 17 , according to its price announcement . The same day, prices for Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, Ground Advantage and Parcel Select would rise an average of 5.9%. The Postal Regulatory Commission will review the changes before they take effect.
The higher fuel surcharges come against a backdrop of higher shipping rates despite consumers’ demand for free shipping. Some sellers have already adjusted their free shipping policies. TickWise 3 Moms Organics, an Indiana maker of natural insect repellent, raised its free-shipping minimum to $100 from $75, founder Lisa-Jae Eggert told Modern Retail in June for its report on brands rewriting shipping policies as fuel costs rise . Her cost to ship a package has climbed to about $8.42 from $5.36, she said.
“Raising those minimum thresholds for free shipping is a necessity,” Eggert said. “It’s not something I want to do.”
The increases land as the Q4 2026 TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index projects ground parcel rates per package will reach a record 43.3% above the index’s January 2018 baseline . The index also found UPS’s increases concentrated among small and midsize customers, FreightWaves’ Eric Kulisch noted as parcel costs neared a record . This comes even as UPS courts small businesses with new digital tools . UPS raises rates an average of 5.9% on Dec. 21 and FedEx follows on Jan. 4, according to Transportation Insight .
Higher minimums carry their own risk
Joe & Bella, which sells adaptive clothing, tested the same move, raising its minimum to $100 from $75. Conversion dropped by more than half, so the company reverted, Modern Retail reported.
“Our site conversion absolutely tanked,” co-founder and CEO Jimmy Zollo told Modern Retail.
Other retailers are changing what shoppers see at checkout. Lori’s Designer Shoes dropped its flat $10 fee on orders under $150 and switched to calculated shipping, footwear buyer Matt Andre said in the same report. Todd Shelton now subtracts return shipping from customers’ refunds, a first for his 23-year-old men’s clothing company in New Jersey, CNBC reported in its look at small retailers bracing for holiday shipping costs .
Makers absorb the label cost
Makers who buy labels one at a time have less room to move. When Jenni Shields opened Evie Pearl Handmade, her hair accessories shop, eight years ago, a label cost her $2.93, she told CNBC. Her average label ran about $4.50 last year and nearly $6 at the post office counter in October. She charges customers $6 for shipping, about $1.50 of it for packaging.
“I am losing money at this point, and I’ve really taken a huge hit this year,” Shields told CNBC. “I can’t compete with Amazon on the free shipping. I can’t do that. I can’t afford that.”
Marketplace sellers are making the same point on X. Replying to an Oct. 23 post about eBay’s USPS label changes, the account Rip and Ship Report wrote, “label goes up, margin shrinks, and you never touched a thing.”
For some sellers, postage is one line in a longer list of costs. Jeffrey Hitte posted on X on Nov. 12 that he had closed his Etsy shop, citing its listing, renewal, transaction and processing fees and ad fees he said he could not opt out of. Etsy charges a 6.5% transaction fee on the item price plus shipping, according to its fee policy . Shops under $10,000 in annual sales can opt out of its 15% Offsite Ads fee , while larger shops must participate at 12%.
“You stopped being a marketplace for makers and became a toll booth. Goodbye,” Hitte wrote.
USPS adds its first fuel fee
FedEx and UPS have charged fuel surcharges for years and have reset their tables to keep those fees elevated even when diesel falls. USPS had not. The agency proposed the 8% charge in March as fuel prices climbed, and it took effect April 26 on Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, Ground Advantage and Parcel Select.
“We have steadfastly avoided surcharges and this charge is less than one-third of what our competitors charge for fuel alone,” the Postal Service said in its March 25 announcement .
USPS then layered holiday prices on top from Oct. 4 through Jan. 17. A retail Ground Advantage package of up to 3 pounds costs 50 cents more in Zones 1 through 4 and 75 cents more in Zones 5 through 9, according to the agency’s holiday price notice .
The holiday prices end Jan. 17, when the 11% surcharge replaces the 8% charge. USPS said it will reevaluate the surcharge in July 2027 based on fuel prices in the first half of the year.
Small businesses raise prices as costs climb
A net 33% of small-business owners raised average selling prices in October, and a net 37% plan increases in the next three months, the highest reading since July 2022, according to the NFIB Small Business Economic Trends report for October . The survey does not ask about shipping, but owners’ written comments in the report do.
“Shipping costs are a killer for my business,” one Pennsylvania professional services owner wrote.
In a September survey of 1,600 decision-makers at U.S. businesses with fewer than 500 employees, ShipStation’s Q4 2026 Shipping Insights Report found that 52% named rising carrier fees and fuel surcharges as a major difficulty, up from 31% in its previous survey. Seventy-two percent said shipping and freight costs climbed in the past three months. ShipStation sells shipping software to small merchants.
Scale decides who can absorb it. Jason Miller, a supply chain management professor at Michigan State University, told TheStreet in an interview on holiday shipping costs for Main Street retailers that because of carrier fuel surcharges, “many smaller merchants are not gonna be able to offer” free delivery.
Some sellers hold their shipping rates
Not every seller is passing the increase along. Sarah Melendy, who sells honey through Mountain Thyme Honey and Gifts in Troutville, Virginia, charges a flat $10 for shipping and plans to keep it through the holidays, she told Roanoke station WDBJ7 for its report on holiday shipping prices for local sellers .
“I have seen an increase in prices, but not so drastic that it’s, you know, going to ruin my business,” Melendy said.
For one seller, the question heading into peak is whether to reopen at all. The seller, who posts as @goldfishinabag_, wrote on X on Nov. 8 that the shop remains closed.
“i would really like to reopen my shop by december but shipping prices have gone up so much i don’t feel good about charging my awesome lovely kind customers for these exorbitant prices,” the seller wrote.
Why it matters: Small Etsy and eBay sellers must reset free-shipping minimums and label pricing before Jan. 17, when USPS makes its fuel surcharge permanent at 11% and raises Ground Advantage rates 5.9%. Those who don’t will absorb higher costs or risk lower conversion heading into peak.
